title: Keggin-Type H₅PMo₁₀V₂O₄₀ Intercalated MgAl-LDH: Structural Integrity and Bifunctional Electrocatalytic Activity
authors: Pushparaj Loganathan, Sunaja Devi K R*, Devaraj Muthukumar
highlightMetric: HER 215 mV / OER 411 mV @ 10 mA cm⁻²
abstract: The study focuses on overcoming the high solubility limitations of discrete polyoxometalates (POMs) by quantitatively intercalating Keggin-type H₅PMo₁₀V₂O₄₀ into MgAl-layered double hydroxide (MgAl-LDH) gallery hosts via a formamide-assisted exfoliation-reassembly route. The resulting POM@MgAl-LDH hybrid expands basal spacing to 9.2–10.5 Å and acts as an exceptionally stable, non-precious bifunctional electrocatalyst for overall alkaline water splitting in 1.0 M KOH, achieving hydrogen and oxygen evolution overpotentials of 215 mV and 411 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² with ~97% current retention over 12 hours.
keyFindings: Quantitative ion-exchange intercalation of Keggin POM clusters expanding LDH basal spacing to 9.2–10.5 Å
DFT calculations supporting highly favorable intercalation thermodynamics (ΔE ≈ −2.3 eV per formula unit)
Bifunctional alkaline water splitting electrocatalyst (HER η = 215 mV, OER η = 411 mV @ 10 mA cm⁻²)
Robust electrocatalytic stability retaining 97% initial current over 12 h continuous operation

title: Utilizing Highly Reactive Lewis Pairs Generated by Oxygen Vacancies in the Cu₃Mo₂O₉ Solid Catalyst for Cycloaddition of CO₂ to 1,2-Propanediol
shortTitle: Oxygen-Vacancy Lewis Pairs in Cu₃Mo₂O₉ for CO₂ Fixation
authors: S. Sujith, B. J. Vaishnavi, K. M. Rajashekhar Vaibhava, Sunaja Devi K R*, Ganapati V. Shanbhag
abstract: Presents engineered Cu₃Mo₂O₉ solid oxide catalyst featuring high-density oxygen vacancies that generate highly active Lewis acid-base pair sites. Synthesized via an ethanol-PEG-400 route at 500 °C, the catalyst stabilizes metastable Mo⁵⁺ and Cu⁺ cations essential for CO₂ activation. It drives solvent-free cycloaddition of CO₂ and 1,2-propanediol into valuable cyclic propylene carbonate with high efficiency, stability, and recyclability.
keyFindings: Engineered oxygen-vacancy-rich Cu₃Mo₂O₉ solid catalyst generating reactive Lewis pair active sites
Stabilization of metastable Mo⁵⁺ and Cu⁺ cations critical for inert CO₂ molecule activation
Direct conversion of CO₂ and 1,2-propanediol into value-added propylene carbonate
Sustained catalytic performance and structural integrity across multiple reaction cycles

title: Harnessing MOF Derived Frustrated Lewis Pair-CeO₂ Nano Catalyst for CO₂-Activated Soft Oxidation of Furfural to Furoic Acid
shortTitle: MOF-Derived CeO₂ FLP Nanocatalyst for CO₂ Soft Oxidation
authors: S. Sujith, Sunaja Devi K R*, Ganapati V. Shanbhag
abstract: Pioneers the use of CO₂ as a mild 'soft oxidant' for green furfural oxidation into furoic acid utilizing a MOF-derived CeO₂ nanocatalyst with rich Frustrated Lewis Pairs (FLPs). The abundant surface oxygen vacancies and metastable Ce³⁺ ions optimize substrate bi-coordination (η²-(C,O) mode) and CO₂ activation, delivering unprecedented 99.9% conversion and 99.9% furoic acid selectivity with high turnover numbers and zero leaching.
keyFindings: First report of CO₂ as a soft oxidant for biomass-derived furfural oxidation to furoic acid
MOF-derived CeO₂ nanocatalyst with high concentration of surface Ce³⁺ / oxygen vacancy FLP sites
Unmatched catalytic activity achieving 99.9% conversion and 99.9% furoic acid selectivity
Mechanistic validation via FTIR adsorption and active-site masking strategies

title: ZIF-8/LDH Nanohybrids for Dye Adsorption: LDH Composition-Dependent Structure and Adsorption Performance
shortTitle: ZIF-8/LDH Interfacial Nanohybrids for Water Purification
authors: Pushparaj Loganathan, Sunaja Devi K R*, Marimuthu Priyadarshini, Cheriyan John, Sankar
highlightMetric: 94% Malachite Green Dye Removal in 60 min
abstract: Investigates in-situ grown ZIF-8/LDH nanohybrids for rapid organic dye pollutant remediation. Demonstrates that LDH cation composition (MgAl vs CaAl) controls nanoscale interfacial structure, with ZIF-8/CaAl-LDH achieving 94% removal of Malachite Green dye within 60 minutes. Multi-mode synergy combining electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, and micropore filling drives rapid kinetics and high structural stability.
keyFindings: In-situ growth strategy for ZIF-8 MOF on layered double hydroxide (LDH) host nanosheets
Composition-dependent interfacial tuning revealing superior adsorption kinetics for CaAl-LDH
Rapid 94% Malachite Green (MG) dye removal efficiency within 60 minutes
Multi-mode synergistic mechanism: electrostatic attraction, H-bonding, and pore filling
